extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and students of patent law
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and procedural criteria for obtaining, maintaining, and enforcing patents across multiple national systems (United States, Spain, Austria, Belgium, France) as described in a 19th-century treatise. Covers patentable subject-matter, specification/enabling-disclosure requirements, filing practice, fees, assignment/registration, infringement remedies, and grounds for cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement patent vs original inventor rights (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: He may have a patent for the improvement, but he is not at liberty to make, use, or vend the original discovery, and the first inventor is not at liberty to use the improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that improvement patents do not permit practicing the prior patented invention and the original patentee cannot automatically use the improvement; establishes limits on mutual freedom-to-operate between original and improvement patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor changes not constitute discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply changing the form or the proportions of any machine, or composition of matter, in any degree, is not to be deemed a discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express prohibition on trivial/formal variations (changes of form, proportions, ornaments) qualifying as patentable inventions; used repeatedly in multiple jurisdictions to exclude purely ornamental or insignificant modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must enable and distinguish (US general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A schedule is appended to the letters patent. It is a written description of the invention, and the manner of using, or the process of compounding the same, in such full, clear, and exact terms as to distinguish the same from all other things before known, and to enable any person skilled in the art or science ... to make, compound, and use the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires full, clear, exact written disclosure sufficient both to identify what is new (distinguish from prior art) and to enable a skilled practitioner to carry out the invention; applies to machines and compositions with additional specific requirements (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine specification must explain principle and modes
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of any machine, the inventor must fully explain the principle, and the several modes in which he has contemplated the application of that principle or character, by which it may be distinguished from other inventions; and he must accompany the whole with drawings and written references, where the nature of the case admits of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For machines, specification must disclose the inventive principle and contemplated applications/modes and include drawings and references when practicable so the invention is distinguished and understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition-of-matter specification and specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention is a composition of matter, the inventor must accompany the specification with specimens of the ingredients and of the composition of the matter, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical/composition inventions the disclosure may require physical specimens (when practicable) to permit meaningful experimentation and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model delivery if required (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: He must also deliver a model of his machine, if the Secretary of State should deem such model to be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require a physical model for understanding/examining the invention; models are conditional and discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification signature and attestation (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description (specification) must be signed by the inventor, and attested by two witnesses, and filed in the office of the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal execution requirements for filing the specification include inventor signature and two witness attestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural filing steps and fees (US practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor begins by paying thirty dollars into the treasury, and taking two receipts. At the Secretary of State's Office he deposits one of those receipts and presents a petition, praying that a patent may be granted for his invention, of which it contains a short description (title). He also makes an affidavit or affirmation that he verily believes that he is the true inventor ... and that he has resided more than two years last past in America (if alien). The Attorney General must within fifteen days certify whether they are conformable to law, and return them to the Secretary, who causes the seal of the United States to be fixed, and records them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies initial payment, petition content (short title), inventor's oath/affidavit (including alien/residence rules), and administrative review steps (AG certification within 15 days), recording and sealing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat / interference arbitration (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of interfering applications from two persons, the same are submitted to the arbitration of three persons, one chosen by each applicant and the third by the Secretary of State. If more than two applicants and they do not agree, the Secretary appoints all three arbitrators. Their award is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes tribunal composition and finality of decisions in cases of competing claims to the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments must be recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, his executor or administrator, may assign the title and interest in the invention at any time: and the assignees may pass it to other persons to any degree. The assignments must be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys requirement to record transfers of patent title to establish public notice and formalize property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement remedies and defenses (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any one infringe the patent, he may be sued by the patentee or his assigns for three times the actual damage sustained. The defendant may plead the general issue and give any special matter ... as that the specification does not contain the whole truth, or that it contains more than is necessary to produce the effect, for the purpose of deceiving the public — that it was not original, but had been in use — or that the patentee had surreptitiously obtained a patent for the discovery of another person; in either of which cases judgment is to be given for the defendant, and the patent declared to be void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides treble damages remedy and enumerates substantive defenses that may void the patent (insufficiency, overstatement, lack of novelty, surreptitious procurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official copies as evidence and fees (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the specification, from the Secretary of State's office, is made competent evidence in all courts touching the patent right. For all copies of papers, the person obtaining them must pay 20 cents for every sheet of 100 words, and two dollars for every copy of a drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies evidentiary weight of office-certified copies and attendant copy fees for litigation or other uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for motions to cancel (US)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion may be made before the Judges of the district court, that the patent was obtained surreptitiously, or upon false suggestion, within three years after the issuing of the said patent, but not afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets three-year window after issue to seek cancellation on grounds of surreptitious procurement/false suggestion (district court jurisdiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish inventor eligibility and no prior novelty examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, of whatever condition or country, who proposes to establish any new invention, may have a Royal Patent of Privilege, without previous examination of the novelty or utility of the object; but without the concession of the grant being considered in any way as a recognition of the novelty or utility of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spain issues privileges without pre-grant novelty/utility examination; grant itself does not constitute a finding of novelty or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish subject matter categories and introduction vs invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of a patent may be any machine, apparatus, instrument, or a mechanical or chemical process or operation, which may be wholly or in part new, or which may not have been established in the same manner and form in the kingdom. If the subject has not been practised in Spain, nor in any foreign country, then the privilege will be given by a Patent of Invention, but if it have been practised abroad, then the party will have a Patent of Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between patents for wholly new inventions and for introduction of foreign-practiced inventions; scope includes machines, apparatus, instruments, and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish specification precision and plan/model requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When the petition for a patent is presented it must be accompanied with a plan or model, and a description or explanation of the invention, specifying what is the peculiar mechanism or process which is presented therein, as not having been hitherto practised; the whole being stated with the greatest precision and clearness, so that there may be at any time no doubt as to the identity of the invention, and of that peculiarity which is represented as hitherto unpractised in that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes precision and clarity to prevent doubt as to identity and novelty; sealed packet practice and duty payments also required before issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanish grounds for cessation/voidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent is declared to be void — 1. When the time is elapsed. 2. When the party does not apply for it within three months from the time he presented his petition. 3. When the patent has not been put in force for a year and a day after the date thereof. 4. When the patentee abandons his right by not using it for a year and a day. 5. When the subject has been used in any part of the kingdom, or described in printed books, or in engravings, pictures, models, plans, or descriptions, contained in the Royal Conservatory of Arts; or when the subject has been used in a foreign country and the patentee has presented it as new and of his own invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists temporal, use, and novelty-related grounds that invalidate Spanish patents; publication or prior use domestically or abroad (if claimed as new) defeats validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian definitions of discovery/invention/improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Every new finding out of a process in industry... 2. Every production of a new object by new means, or of a new object by means already known, or the production of an object already known, by means different from those which have hitherto been used... 3. Every addition of a preparation, arrangement, or method of working to a process already known... shall be held to be an improvement. 4. Every discovery, invention, improvement, or change shall be held as new, if it is not known in the monarchy, either in practice or by a description of it contained in a work publicly printed. But the novelty ... shall not be called in question on account of its being described in a work publicly printed, unless that description is so accurate and clear that any person acquainted with the subject can ... manufacture the object, or practise the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definitions include rediscovered processes, new objects by new or known means, improvements that increase success or economy; printed prior art only defeats novelty if enabling in the jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian specification formal and sufficiency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must send in ... a sealed parcel containing an accurate description ... with the following qualifications: (1) written in German or local business language; (2) drawn up so clearly that every person who understands the subject may be able to manufacture the object ... without being obliged to supply any further inventions, additions, or improvements; (3) that which is new must be accurately distinguished and set forth; (4) clearly and distinctly described without ambiguities; (5) nothing must be kept secret, either in the materials or the method of execution; essential manipulations must not be concealed; drawings and models to be added if practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines language, enablement, precise identification of novel features, prohibition on concealment of essential means, and optional drawings/models as sufficiency criteria for Austrian patent descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian practice: petition, sealed description, and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition is first presented ... with a full description of the invention sealed up. He must at the same time deposit one-half of the duty payable for the patent. The direction ... forwards the money and documents ... to the Imperial Board of Commerce. The patent is made out and delivered to the inventor. Duties are paid in proportion to the time granted ... one half of the duty ... is paid on receipt of the petition, and the other half at the beginning of each year, under pain of its being annulled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes sealed-packet filing, staged fee payments tied to term, administrative review, and annulment risk for nonpayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian grounds for annulment/voidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The privilege becomes void, 1. If the accurate description ... is wanting in the requisites ... 2. If any one proves legally, that the privileged discovery ... could not be considered new in the monarchy, previous to the date of the official certificate. 3. If the possessor of a privilege in force for a discovery ... proves that the privilege subsequently granted is identically the same as his own ... 4. If the privileged person has not began to practise his discovery, invention, or improvement, within the term of one year from the delivery of his privilege. 5. If he discontinues that practice for the space of a year, during the term of the privilege, without showing sufficient grounds. 6. If the second half of the tax is not paid in the above stated annual rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates specification sufficiency, novelty, prior priority, working/use, discontinuance, and fee-payment grounds for annulment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belgian requirement: sealed detailed description and penalties for fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must send with his petition a sealed packet containing an exact and detailed description, signed by himself, of the object or the secret for which the patent is solicited, together with the necessary plans and drawings. If he fraudulently omit in the description to mention any part of his secret, or shall state it falsely, or if the object has been already described in any work printed or published, then the patent becomes void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes completeness and honesty in the sealed specification; omission or falsity or prior printed disclosure voids the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belgian practice: nonpublication until expiry and registry
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification or description ... sealed up, must accompany the petition; which is not to be published until the expiration of the term of the patent; and not even then if the government, for important reasons, should think it necessary to defer the publication. A Register is kept ... and he who takes a patent by right of succession must register his name before he attempts to use the invention; and notice of all patents are given in the official journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes confidentiality of sealed descriptions pre-grant, government control of publication timing, and mandatory registration for successors before exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belgian scope and duration rules; obligations to manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for five, ten, or fifteen years; they may be prolonged from five or ten to fifteen years. But patents for the introduction or application of inventions or improvements made in foreign countries ... are not granted for a longer time than that during which the exclusive right in such foreign countries for those objects shall last; and they contain an express clause that the objects shall be manufactured in the kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits terms for importation patents to foreign term and may require domestic manufacture as a condition of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belgian grounds for voidance: use obligations and secrecy/dangerousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent is void if the specification is not given as above stated. It also becomes void if the patentee does not use his invention within the space of two years from the date of his patent, unless there have been strong reasons for that delay ... A patentee invalidates his grant if he subsequently obtains a patent for the same invention in a foreign country. If the invention ... is dangerous to the security of the kingdom or its inhabitants, it may be ordered to be cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies nonuse, duplicative foreign patents, and public-safety grounds as bases for cancellation; government assesses 'strong reasons' for delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: French patent terms and inventor conception principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for five, ten, or fifteen years, according to the choice of the inventor, for any discovery or new invention in all kinds of industry. The National Assembly stated ... that every new idea ... belongs originally to him who has conceived it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: France recognizes inventor's original rights and offers selectable terms (5/10/15 years) with extension possibilities under legislature for longer terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: French prohibition on concealing real means; exact description required
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent is forfeited if the inventor conceal his real means of execution; or if he uses any secret means which were not detailed in his description of the invention. That description must be an exact account of the principles and the means and processes which constitute the discovery, and must be accompanied with such plans, sections, drawings, and models, which may be required to explain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates full disclosure of operative means; concealment of essential execution means or reliance on secret measures voids the patent; drawings/models required as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: French practice: sealed packet, two copies list, publicity and inspection rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must ... deposit in a sealed packet an exact description ... The petitioner must make two copies of the list of papers in the sealed packet. He is entitled to have information given to him of all subjects for which patents have been obtained ... The Directory of Patents, after registering the packet, open the seal, and deliver out a patent containing the description of the invention under their own seal. A register is kept ... Any citizen may inspect the catalogue of new inventions ... and any resident citizen is at liberty to examine the specifications of the patents actually in force ... unless the legislature has decreed that the discovery shall be kept secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes sealed-packet deposit, internal registry, limited pre-grant inspection rights, post-issue inspection of patents in force except for legislatively-declared secrets, and administrative publication/proclamation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: French fee payment schedule and forfeiture for nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: The duties collected from an inventor may be paid in two sums— one half on presenting his petition, and the remainder within six months. If the latter sum is not paid within that time, the patent becomes void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies staged payment of duties with forfeiture risk for missed second installment; detailed fee scales provided for different term lengths and services.
